title: Backend batch 1: mail/file status codes, intake timing-safe comparison, auth-refusal logging

approvals.evidence: auto-approved: no protected path (app/api/**/route.ts, lib/authLog.ts only), no migration, no schema change

body.design_ref: None -- no open design question; the status-code fix follows RFC 9110 semantics already used elsewhere in this codebase (e.g. the 409 on a refused persistActions call in other routes), the timing-safe comparison mirrors the existing lib/auth/seal.ts pattern verbatim, and the logging helper mirrors the one refusal already logged in app/api/auth/callback/route.ts.

steps.title: app/api/mail/file/route.ts: set status 409 on the dedupe-conflict response, status 409 on create-refused, status 404 on issue-not-found, status 409 on attach-refused. Confirm components/InboxPanel.tsx reads data.ok from the parsed body, not res.ok/status.
app/api/intake/route.ts: import timingSafeEqual from node:crypto; compare the bearer token via a length check followed by timingSafeEqual instead of !==, mirroring lib/auth/seal.ts.
Add lib/authLog.ts: logAuthRefusal(route, reason, actor) writing one console.warn line. No dependency on request/session internals so it is trivially unit-safe.
Wire logAuthRefusal into the 5 named 401/403 sites in app/api/mail/file/route.ts, excluding the deliberately-scoped-out 'reconnect your inbox' 401.
Wire logAuthRefusal into the remaining 8 named 401/403 sites across app/api/workspace/route.ts, app/api/mail/send/route.ts, app/api/documents/route.ts and app/api/documents/[id]/route.ts.
steps.verify_command: npx tsc --noEmit && npm run audit:a11y && npm run audit:tenancy && npm run audit:attribution && npm run audit:contracts && npm run validate:scenarios

commit_boundaries: All five steps as one commit: three independent findings on non-overlapping concerns (status codes, one cipher call, one logging call), each low-risk in isolation, closed together because they share one review, one verification run, and one PR.
body.rollback: Revert the single commit. Step 2 carries the only step where a coding mistake could break the intake endpoint outright (e.g. a length check that rejects a correct token); verified against the existing reference implementation in lib/auth/seal.ts and against the full validate:scenarios suite, which already exercises intake's classify/refuse paths.
